claim: Splitting 100.00 three ways gives 33.33, 33.33 and 33.34, and splitting a refund of -100.00 gives -33.34, -33.34 and -33.32. Both sets of shares add back up to the original amount.
why: split.shares uses floor division, which rounds toward minus infinity, so the base share of -10000 cents is -3334 and the last share takes the remainder -3332. Running main.py prints exactly these shares and both sums. The trap is expecting the refund to mirror the charge, as truncation toward zero would give.
